name: Study ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **study id** for this study: One stable unique identifier for the included paper. (Purpose: Unique key linking the same study across all tabs.) NOTE: Use exactly the same Study ID in all worksheets.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Use exactly the same Study ID in all worksheets.

name: First Author
prompt: From this study, identify the **first author** for this study: Surname of the first listed author. (Purpose: Basic study identification.) NOTE: Use only the surname unless disambiguation is needed.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Use only the surname unless disambiguation is needed.

name: Publication Year
prompt: From this study, identify the **publication year** for this study: Year the paper was published. (Purpose: Basic study identification.) NOTE: Use the main publication year shown in the article.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Integer. 4-digit year.
notes: Use the main publication year shown in the article.

name: Country
prompt: From this study, identify the **country** for this study: Country or countries where the study was conducted. (Purpose: Study context.) NOTE: Keep concise. Use NR if not reported.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Keep concise. Use NR if not reported.

name: Study Design (Reported)
prompt: From this study, identify the **study design (reported)** for this study: The study design label that best fits the article. (Purpose: Captures the design actually used in the paper.) Choose exactly one of: cross_sectional, cohort, case_control, diagnostic_accuracy, interventional_nonrandomized, randomized, case_series, other, NR. NOTE: Choose the most defensible reported design; do not over-interpret.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: cross_sectional; cohort; case_control; diagnostic_accuracy; interventional_nonrandomized; randomized; case_series; other; NR
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Choose the most defensible reported design; do not over-interpret.

name: Study Setting
prompt: From this study, identify the **study setting** for this study: A short description of the setting. (Purpose: Provides context for how/where the study was done.) NOTE: Examples: single center; multicenter; tertiary referral center.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Examples: single center; multicenter; tertiary referral center.

name: Study ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **study id** for this cohort/group: Study ID exactly as used in Study_Level. (Purpose: Links this row back to the study.) NOTE: Must match a Study_Level row exactly.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Must match a Study_Level row exactly.

name: Cohort ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **cohort id** for this cohort/group: One unique identifier for this cohort/method row. (Purpose: Unique key for each extractable cohort or group.) NOTE: Create one row per analyzable cohort/group-method combination.
constraints: Free text, must be **unique** within its scope. Format: Text.
notes: Create one row per analyzable cohort/group-method combination.

name: Cohort/Group Role
prompt: From this study, identify the **cohort/group role** for this cohort/group: The analytic role of the cohort/group. (Purpose: Clarifies what this group represents within the study.) Choose exactly one of: overall, disease, control, comparator, subgroup, other, not_separable, NR. NOTE: Use not_separable when subgroup-specific extraction is not possible.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: overall; disease; control; comparator; subgroup; other; not_separable; NR
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use not_separable when subgroup-specific extraction is not possible.

name: Review Disease Group
prompt: From this study, identify the **review disease group** for this cohort/group: The prespecified disease category used in this review. (Purpose: Places the cohort into the review's disease taxonomy.) NOTE: This is a review-level harmonized category, not necessarily the paper's exact wording.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Category.
notes: This is a review-level harmonized category, not necessarily the paper's exact wording.

name: Age Group
prompt: From this study, identify the **age group** for this cohort/group: The age category for the cohort. (Purpose: Supports age-based subgrouping.) Choose exactly one of: pediatric, adult, mixed, unclear. NOTE: Use unclear when the paper does not allow a safe classification.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `unclear` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use unclear when the paper does not allow a safe classification.

name: Sample Size (Reported)
prompt: From this study, identify the **sample size (reported)** for this cohort/group: The total number of participants in that cohort/group. (Purpose: Captures the reported cohort size.) NOTE: Use the group size as reported, not the analyzed n for a specific outcome.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Integer. Integer. Must be >= 1.
notes: Use the group size as reported, not the analyzed n for a specific outcome.

name: Age, Central Value (years)
prompt: From this study, identify the **age, central value (years)** for this cohort/group: Mean or median age in years, exactly as reported. (Purpose: Provides a summary age measure for the cohort.) NOTE: Do not convert medians to means.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Do not convert medians to means.

name: Female (%)
prompt: From this study, identify the **female (%)** for this cohort/group: Percent female in the cohort. (Purpose: Captures sex distribution.) NOTE: Enter a percentage. Derive only when the paper gives enough exact information.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Percentage. Range 0-100.
notes: Enter a percentage. Derive only when the paper gives enough exact information.

name: MRI Modality
prompt: From this study, identify the **mri modality** for this cohort/group: The MRI modality used for CVR mapping in that row. (Purpose: Main imaging stratifier.) Choose exactly one of: BOLD, ASL, BOLD+ASL, other, NR. NOTE: Split rows if the study reports separate results by modality.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Split rows if the study reports separate results by modality.

name: Field Strength (T)
prompt: From this study, identify the **field strength (t)** for this cohort/group: MRI field strength in Tesla. (Purpose: Scanner descriptor.) Choose exactly one of: 1.5, 3, 7, other, NR. NOTE: Use a single value when one scanner strength applies to the row.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use a single value when one scanner strength applies to the row.

name: CVR Stimulus
prompt: From this study, identify the **cvr stimulus** for this cohort/group: The actual CVR stimulus/challenge type. (Purpose: Identifies what physiological challenge was used.) Choose exactly one of: CO2, acetazolamide, breath_hold, paced_breathing, resting_state, mixed, other, NR. NOTE: This is the stimulus itself, not how it was delivered.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: CO2; acetazolamide; breath_hold; paced_breathing; resting_state; mixed; other; NR
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: This is the stimulus itself, not how it was delivered.

name: Stimulus Delivery Method
prompt: From this study, identify the **stimulus delivery method** for this cohort/group: The delivery/administration method used for the CVR challenge. (Purpose: Captures how the stimulus was administered.) Choose exactly one of: end_tidal_forcing, fixed_inspired_gas, sequential_gas_delivery, breath_hold_task, paced_breathing_task, acetazolamide_challenge, resting_state_no_external_stimulus, other, NR. NOTE: Separate this from CVR Stimulus. Example: stimulus = CO2, delivery = end_tidal_forcing.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: end_tidal_forcing; fixed_inspired_gas; sequential_gas_delivery; breath_hold_task; paced_breathing_task; acetazolamide_challenge; resting_state_no_external_stimulus; other; NR
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Separate this from CVR Stimulus. Example: stimulus = CO2, delivery = end_tidal_forcing.

name: Physiology Monitoring
prompt: From this study, identify the **physiology monitoring** for this cohort/group: The best-fitting monitoring category for CO2/physiology capture. (Purpose: Captures the rigor of physiologic monitoring.) Choose exactly one of: continuous_EtCO2_synchronized, continuous_EtCO2_not_synchronized_or_unclear, limited_or_intermittent_CO2_monitoring, no_CO2_monitoring_surrogate_only, NR. NOTE: Use the category that best matches what the paper clearly reports.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use the category that best matches what the paper clearly reports.

name: Baseline EtCO2 (mmHg)
prompt: From this study, identify the **baseline etco2 (mmhg)** for this cohort/group: Baseline end-tidal CO2 in mmHg. (Purpose: Baseline physiology descriptor.) NOTE: Use NA when baseline EtCO2 does not apply or is not conceptually relevant to the paradigm.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Use NA when baseline EtCO2 does not apply or is not conceptually relevant to the paradigm.

name: Achieved ΔEtCO2 (mmHg)
prompt: From this study, identify the **achieved δetco2 (mmhg)** for this cohort/group: Reported achieved change in end-tidal CO2 in mmHg. (Purpose: Change in CO2 exposure.) NOTE: Use NA when the study design does not involve a measurable EtCO2 change.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Use NA when the study design does not involve a measurable EtCO2 change.

name: TR (ms)
prompt: From this study, identify the **tr (ms)** for this cohort/group: Repetition time in milliseconds. (Purpose: Core acquisition parameter.) NOTE: Record the exact reported value.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Record the exact reported value.

name: TE (ms)
prompt: From this study, identify the **te (ms)** for this cohort/group: Echo time in milliseconds. (Purpose: Core acquisition parameter.) NOTE: Record the exact reported value.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Record the exact reported value.

name: Voxel Size (Reported)
prompt: From this study, identify the **voxel size (reported)** for this cohort/group: Voxel dimensions exactly as reported. (Purpose: Core acquisition parameter.) NOTE: Keep the paper's reported format, e.g., 3 x 3 x 5 mm.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Keep the paper's reported format, e.g., 3 x 3 x 5 mm.

name: Scan Duration (s)
prompt: From this study, identify the **scan duration (s)** for this cohort/group: Total acquisition duration in seconds. (Purpose: Core acquisition parameter.) NOTE: Convert minutes to seconds only when the conversion is explicit and safe.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Convert minutes to seconds only when the conversion is explicit and safe.

name: Brain Coverage
prompt: From this study, identify the **brain coverage** for this cohort/group: The reported spatial coverage category. (Purpose: Captures spatial extent of the acquisition.) Choose exactly one of: whole_brain, partial_brain_multislice, single_slice, territory_targeted, other, NR. NOTE: Classify coverage based on what is reported, not what you infer from the images.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: whole_brain; partial_brain_multislice; single_slice; territory_targeted; other; NR
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Classify coverage based on what is reported, not what you infer from the images.

name: CVR Modeling Approach
prompt: From this study, identify the **cvr modeling approach** for this cohort/group: The dominant modeling/analysis family used for CVR estimation. (Purpose: Captures the main analysis framework used to derive CVR.) Choose exactly one of: GLM, linear_regression, correlation_based, frequency_domain, resting_state_model, other, not_reported. NOTE: Choose the main approach used for the reported result.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: GLM; linear_regression; correlation_based; frequency_domain; resting_state_model; other; not_reported
missing: Use `not_reported` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Choose the main approach used for the reported result.

name: Lag/Delay Correction
prompt: From this study, identify the **lag/delay correction** for this cohort/group: The lag/delay correction approach used, if any. (Purpose: Important harmonization variable.) Choose exactly one of: voxelwise_lag_or_delay_corrected, ROI_level_corrected, fixed_shift_only, none, other, not_reported. NOTE: This field is important for cross-study harmonization and subgrouping.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: voxelwise_lag_or_delay_corrected; ROI_level_corrected; fixed_shift_only; none; other; not_reported
missing: Use `not_reported` / `none` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: This field is important for cross-study harmonization and subgrouping.

name: Spatial Smoothing
prompt: From this study, identify the **spatial smoothing** for this cohort/group: Whether spatial smoothing was reported for the analysis. (Purpose: Captures whether smoothing was used.) Choose exactly one of: reported, not_reported, unclear. NOTE: Use unclear only when the paper is ambiguous.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `unclear` / `not_reported` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use unclear only when the paper is ambiguous.

name: QA/QC Maps Reported
prompt: From this study, identify the **qa/qc maps reported** for this cohort/group: Whether QA or QC maps were explicitly reported, shown, or stated. (Purpose: Captures explicit quality-control reporting.) Choose exactly one of: yes, no, NR. NOTE: Use yes only when QA/QC maps are clearly presented or described.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `NR` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use yes only when QA/QC maps are clearly presented or described.

name: Protocol Reproducibility Judgment
prompt: From this study, identify the **protocol reproducibility judgment** for this cohort/group: Best overall judgment of protocol reproducibility based on the reported methods. (Purpose: Captures whether the reported CVR protocol is reproducible in practice.) Choose exactly one of: sufficient, partial, insufficient, unclear. NOTE: Base the judgment on stimulus, delivery, physiology monitoring, acquisition, and processing details. Use “unclear” if the report is too ambiguous for a confident assessment.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: Use `unclear` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Base the judgment on stimulus, delivery, physiology monitoring, acquisition, and processing details. Use “unclear” if the report is too ambiguous for a confident assessment.

name: Study ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **study id** for this specific result/estimate: Study ID exactly as used in Study_Level. (Purpose: Links this row back to the study.) NOTE: Must match a Study_Level row exactly.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Must match a Study_Level row exactly.

name: Outcome ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **outcome id** for this specific result/estimate: One unique identifier for this outcome row. (Purpose: Unique key for each extracted estimate.) NOTE: Create one row per extractable estimate/result.
constraints: Free text, must be **unique** within its scope. Format: Text.
notes: Create one row per extractable estimate/result.

name: Cohort ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **cohort id** for this specific result/estimate: Cohort ID exactly as used in Cohort_Methods. (Purpose: Links the result to the source cohort row.) NOTE: Must match a Cohort_Methods row exactly.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Must match a Cohort_Methods row exactly.

name: Comparator Cohort ID
prompt: From this study, identify the **comparator cohort id** for this specific result/estimate: Comparator Cohort ID when the result is comparative. (Purpose: Links comparative results to a comparator group.) NOTE: Use NA for non-comparative results.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Use NA for non-comparative results.

name: Result Type
prompt: From this study, identify the **result type** for this specific result/estimate: The broad result category for that row. (Purpose: Classifies what kind of result is being extracted.) Choose exactly one of: CVR_summary, CVR_difference, feasibility, lag_delay, reproducibility, other. NOTE: Use the single best-fitting category.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: CVR_summary; CVR_difference; feasibility; lag_delay; reproducibility; other
missing: No explicit missing code in this closed list; if truly unreported, leave blank and flag for review.
notes: Use the single best-fitting category.

name: Specific Outcome Label
prompt: From this study, identify the **specific outcome label** for this specific result/estimate: A short label describing the specific outcome/result. (Purpose: Human-readable label for the exact metric.) NOTE: Example: whole-brain mean CVR; hemispheric CVR asymmetry; failed map rate.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Example: whole-brain mean CVR; hemispheric CVR asymmetry; failed map rate.

name: ROI/Region Category
prompt: From this study, identify the **roi/region category** for this specific result/estimate: The standardized region/ROI category used by the extracted estimate. (Purpose: Standardizes the spatial level of the result.) Choose exactly one of: whole_brain, hemisphere, vascular_territory, lesion_region, voxelwise_distribution, other, NA. NOTE: Use NA only when no ROI/region concept applies.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: whole_brain; hemisphere; vascular_territory; lesion_region; voxelwise_distribution; other; NA
missing: Use `NA` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use NA only when no ROI/region concept applies.

name: CVR Unit (as reported)
prompt: From this study, identify the **cvr unit (as reported)** for this specific result/estimate: The unit exactly as written in the paper. (Purpose: Preserves the paper's original unit expression.) NOTE: Do not harmonize or reinterpret in this field.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Do not harmonize or reinterpret in this field.

name: Standardized Unit Family
prompt: From this study, identify the **standardized unit family** for this specific result/estimate: The review-level standardized unit family. (Purpose: Places different units into a harmonized synthesis family.) Choose exactly one of: percent_signal_change_per_mmHg, CBF_change_per_mmHg, time_based_metric, dimensionless_index, other, NA. NOTE: Use this for synthesis/harmonization across studies.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: percent_signal_change_per_mmHg; CBF_change_per_mmHg; time_based_metric; dimensionless_index; other; NA
missing: Use `NA` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use this for synthesis/harmonization across studies.

name: N Analyzed
prompt: From this study, identify the **n analyzed** for this specific result/estimate: The number of subjects included in that specific analysis. (Purpose: Captures the denominator actually used for that result.) NOTE: This may be smaller than the reported cohort size.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Integer. Integer.
notes: This may be smaller than the reported cohort size.

name: Central Estimate
prompt: From this study, identify the **central estimate** for this specific result/estimate: The primary numeric value for that row. (Purpose: Main quantitative result.) NOTE: Examples: mean, median, rate, or other central summary.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Examples: mean, median, rate, or other central summary.

name: Dispersion Type
prompt: From this study, identify the **dispersion type** for this specific result/estimate: The type of dispersion or uncertainty accompanying the estimate. (Purpose: Captures the form of uncertainty/spread reported.) Choose exactly one of: SD, SE, IQR, 95CI, range, none, NR. NOTE: Use none when dispersion truly does not apply to that result.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
allowed: SD; SE; IQR; 95CI; range; none; NR
missing: Use `NR` / `none` (must be an allowed list value).
notes: Use none when dispersion truly does not apply to that result.

name: Dispersion Value
prompt: From this study, identify the **dispersion value** for this specific result/estimate: The numeric value corresponding to the listed dispersion type. (Purpose: Stores the numeric dispersion value.) NOTE: Use NA when dispersion is not applicable.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Number.
notes: Use NA when dispersion is not applicable.

name: Failed Subjects (n)
prompt: From this study, identify the **failed subjects (n)** for this specific result/estimate: Number of failed, excluded, or unusable subjects reported for that metric. (Purpose: Captures reported failures/exclusions relevant to feasibility.) NOTE: Use only when the paper gives a count tied to the result or mapping process.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Integer. Integer.
notes: Use only when the paper gives a count tied to the result or mapping process.

name: Failure Denominator (n)
prompt: From this study, identify the **failure denominator (n)** for this specific result/estimate: The denominator corresponding to Failed Subjects (n). (Purpose: Provides the denominator for the failure count.) NOTE: Usually attempted scans, total scanned subjects, or the relevant cohort size.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Integer. Integer.
notes: Usually attempted scans, total scanned subjects, or the relevant cohort size.

name: Failure Definition (as reported)
prompt: From this study, identify the **failure definition (as reported)** for this specific result/estimate: The study's own wording for failed/excluded/unusable data. (Purpose: Preserves how the paper defined failure.) NOTE: Keep close to the paper's language; do not over-edit.
constraints: Free text / number as reported. Format: Text.
notes: Keep close to the paper's language; do not over-edit.

name: Meta-analysis Ready?
prompt: From this study, identify the **meta-analysis ready?** for this specific result/estimate: Whether the row is directly usable for meta-analysis without further clarification. (Purpose: Operational flag for immediate quantitative synthesis.) Choose exactly one of: yes, no, maybe_after_author_contact. NOTE: Judge conservatively. Use maybe_after_author_contact only when the missing piece seems recoverable.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: No explicit missing code in this closed list; if truly unreported, leave blank and flag for review.
notes: Judge conservatively. Use maybe_after_author_contact only when the missing piece seems recoverable.

name: Author Contact Needed?
prompt: From this study, identify the **author contact needed?** for this specific result/estimate: Whether an author query would likely recover important missing data. (Purpose: Tracks whether contacting authors may materially help extraction.) Choose exactly one of: yes, no. NOTE: Use yes only when contact could realistically improve extractability or usability.
constraints: Controlled vocabulary (must match a dropdown value exactly). Format: Category.
missing: No explicit missing code in this closed list; if truly unreported, leave blank and flag for review.
notes: Use yes only when contact could realistically improve extractability or usability.
